subject: Help vectorising a hierarchical binomial regression

messages.author: abab84dd2ba42997
messages.subject: Help vectorising a hierarchical binomial regression
parts:
Hello,

First of all, thanks for the great effort at bringing this stuff to the community! Stan is (going to be) great. I had previously played around with JAGS models but found that they were taking ages to converge and producing highly autocorrelated output; Stan by comparison does marvelously.

I am new to Stan, so apologies if this question is redundant. I couldn't find a similar question/answer on the forums. I am mostly fitting hierarchical GLMs to binary data, with two additional parameters to scale the expected values of the sigmoids (upper and lower bounds). This is working great, but in an effort to speed up my code I would like to vectorize where possible. Unfortunately I'm getting quite confused by the documentation so I came here for help.

Short question: can the model given on page 50 of the manual for Hierarchical Logistic Regression (section 10.7, version 1.0.3) be vectorized such that the loop over individual observations (n in 1:N) can be removed?

As I understand it, this would require the creation of a vector of integers (e.g. something like vector[N] int y), which as far as I can see in the documentation is currently not possible (only an array of integers of length N).

My model is approximately the same with a few extra parameters. I can attach a script later if you think it is helpful, but solving this for the model given in section 10.7 would do the trick.

Thanks

Tom Wallis

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Help vectorising a hierarchical binomial regression
parts:
On Friday, December 7, 2012 12:25:03 PM UTC-5, Tom Wallis wrote:
Short question: can the model given on page 50 of the manual for Hierarchical Logistic Regression (section 10.7, version 1.0.3) be vectorized such that the loop over individual observations (n in 1:N) can be removed?

For Stan v1.0.3, I think this is not possible. But it is possible in what will become v1.0.4 in the sense that you could do something like this:

for (n in 1:N) {
  pi[n] <- inv_logit(dot_product(x[n], beta[ll[n]]);
}
y ~ bernoulli(pi);

where pi is a vector[N] that is declared in the model block (won't be saved) or in the transformed parameters block (will be saved). This does not eliminate the loop, but loops are fast in C++ as long as they only involve assignment statements (with <-) and not sampling statements (with ~).

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Help vectorising a hierarchical binomial regression
parts: On Friday, December 7, 2012 12:25:03 PM UTC-5, Tom Wallis wrote:
My model is approximately the same with a few extra parameters. I can attach a script later if you think it is helpful, but solving this for the model given in section 10.7 would do the trick.

The main thing that you would want to modify about the model in section 10.7 is to use the Matt trick for the betas. There will be more documentation for doing so in v1.0.4.

Ben
